name: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc.
moat_justification: Structural cost advantage (operating ratio 70.1% in Q2 2026 vs industry mid-80s) from network density, owned service centers and a non-union low-turnover workforce; service quality (99% on-time, 0.1% claims) converts to pricing power (rev/cwt +5.5% ex-fuel in Q2 2026 with volumes down, 4.9% general rate increase effective Oct 2026); spare capacity and a net-cash balance sheet let it take share through cycles — against low switching costs/annual bids, no network effects, capable rivals (XPO, Saia, FedEx Freight, Estes) investing to close the service gap, and freight cyclicality (revenue -5.5% in FY2025, tons/day still -4.1% in Q2 2026 and -0.9% in Aug 2026).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Strong-moat (7/10) best-in-class LTL carrier with real pricing power and a net-cash balance sheet, but at $183.17 on a normalized base of $4.05/share (2.2% OE yield) it yields a 5.2% weighted IRR — clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$38 (~$30 with a margin of safety); even the super-bull case ($76.22) is far below today's price.
moat_for: Structural cost advantage — operating ratio 70.1% in Q2 2026 vs industry mid-80s
Service quality converts to pricing power — 99% on-time, 0.1% claims, rev/cwt +5.5% ex-fuel in Q2 2026
Network density and owned service centers with spare capacity to take share through cycles
Non-union, low-turnover workforce and through-cycle investment discipline
Net-cash balance sheet funds investment without dilution
moat_against: Low switching costs — LTL sold on annual bids, shippers multi-source, no network effects
Capable rivals XPO, Saia, FedEx Freight and Estes investing to close the service gap
Freight cyclicality — revenue -5.5% in FY2025, tons/day still negative in 2026
Structural cost inflation (driver wages, equipment, real estate) passed through only with a lag
